name: Heparin
high_alert_note: Named among the FDA infusion pump page's examples of high-risk infusions; the local high-alert list governs.
summary: Anticoagulant for prophylaxis and treatment of venous thrombosis and pulmonary embolism and other thrombotic conditions. Nursing focus: strength confusion and fatal medication errors, haemorrhage, heparin-induced thrombocytopenia, and monitoring of coagulation, platelets and potassium.
evidence_type_note: The evidence here is a regulator product label (prescribing information written for prescribers and pharmacists). It is not a bedside nursing practice guideline: the nursing actions are inferences from label warnings, marked partial, and the unit's protocol governs practice.
jurisdiction_note: US FDA label only. EMA, MHRA and SFDA labels were not read; indications, warnings and presentations differ by country and by manufacturer.

sources.use: regulator label sections (boxed warning, indications, warnings, adverse reactions) read in full text
FDA infusion pump page (high-risk infusion examples)

items.text: The label indicates heparin for prophylaxis and treatment of venous thrombosis and pulmonary embolism, prevention of postoperative deep venous thrombosis and pulmonary embolism in selected surgical patients, and other thrombotic uses.
Carefully examine each vial to confirm the correct strength and product before administration.
Monitor platelet count and haematocrit in all patients, and blood coagulation tests guide therapy for full-dose heparin.
Measure blood potassium in patients at risk of hyperkalaemia before starting heparin and periodically in all patients.
The label calls for platelet counts before and periodically during heparin therapy, and for monitoring for signs of heparin-induced thrombocytopenia.
Fatal medication errors: heparin must not be used as a catheter lock flush product, and fatal haemorrhages have occurred when heparin vials were confused with catheter lock flush vials.
Haemorrhage can occur at virtually any site; fatal cases have occurred, so use caution in conditions with increased bleeding risk.
Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia and thrombosis: monitor for signs and discontinue if indicated.
Benzyl-alcohol-preserved products must not be used in neonates and infants.
The label lists haemorrhage and heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (with or without thrombosis) among the clinically significant adverse reactions.
Report any bleeding, a falling platelet count, new thrombosis or a suspected strength or product mix-up immediately.
Record the product and strength check, second-person checks, coagulation and platelet results and escalation per unit standard.
Institution-specific preparation: follow your pharmacy's preparation standard and the product labelling. This library gives no preparation or concentration instructions.
Institution-specific dosing: follow the prescriber's order and your institution's approved protocol. This library gives no dosing instructions.

monitoring.text: Check the vial strength and product against the order before every use.
Watch for bleeding at any site.
Review coagulation tests, platelet count, haematocrit and potassium as ordered.
Report bleeding, a falling platelet count or a suspected product mix-up at once.

gaps: Dosing, concentration, flushes and compatibility: deliberately not included.
